title: Free Chinese AI Models Are Getting Scary Good at Hacking
gist: Benchmarking by Vals finds open-weight models (DeepSeek, 73% task completion) now nearly match the best gated frontier cyber model (OpenAI's Daybreak, 81%) at multi-step network intrusion, at roughly a tenth of the token cost. This suggests that frontier labs' gated-access strategy (Anthropic's Mythos/Project Glasswing) has largely run out of time, roughly on the 6-24 month schedule Anthropic itself predicted.

insights.claim: Vals found that open-weight AI models are now almost as capable as the best closed models at carrying out complex, multi-step intrusions on mock corporate networks.
insights.speaker: Vals
insights.so_what: Offensive cyber capability is spreading beyond the labs, which raises baseline threat levels for every enterprise.
insights.locator: Open-weight artificial intelligence models are now

insights.claim: OpenAI's trusted-partner-only cyber model Daybreak completed 81% of Vals' attack tasks on average across two runs, while China's open-weight DeepSeek completed 73%, and the two scored equally on some tasks.
insights.speaker: Vals
insights.so_what: An 8-point gap is small enough that holding back closed models no longer gives defenders a meaningful edge.
insights.quote: The Chinese open-weight model DeepSeek was not far behind, completing 73 percent of the objectives on average.

insights.claim: A Vals researcher says the best frontier models, available only through trusted access programs, are starting to be matched by open models that anyone can download.
insights.speaker: Nikil Ravi
insights.so_what: Gated release no longer works as a containment strategy.
insights.quote: The best frontier models, locked up inside the labs and available only through trusted access programs, are now starting to be matched by open models

insights.claim: Vals' tests covered two scenarios: a corporate network reached through a public-facing website, and a two-network setup where the model had to compromise one company to pivot into a second.
insights.speaker: Vals
insights.so_what: Lateral-movement and supply-chain-style pivots are now within reach of models anyone can download.
insights.locator: Vals tested AI models in two

insights.claim: Vals estimates an attack run costs $17 to $46 in tokens with GPT-6-Sol versus $2 to $3 with DeepSeek, because open models can run on the user's own hardware.
insights.speaker: Vals
insights.so_what: A roughly 10x cost gap makes mass automated attacks cheap and puts pricing pressure on closed-model API revenue in security work.
insights.quote: it costs $17 to $46 in tokens for GPT-6-Sol to carry out an attack compared to $2 to $3 for DeepSeek

insights.claim: The CEO of Vals argues that the cost gap gives defenders a strong incentive to use open models rather than proprietary ones.
insights.speaker: Rayan Krishnan
insights.so_what: Security vendors may move to self-hosted open models, which cuts into frontier labs' enterprise cyber revenue.

insights.claim: The Vals findings suggest that frontier labs' efforts to limit access to their most capable models, in order to slow the spread of cyber capabilities, may now be moot.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: Undercuts the safety and policy case for restricted releases, and the commercial value of 'trusted access' tiers.

insights.claim: Anthropic started limited releases with Claude Mythos Preview in April, on the premise that gated access through Project Glasswing would only buy defenders time.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: The policy rested on a time window, and that window now appears to have closed.
insights.locator: The findings are also noteworthy given

insights.claim: In April, Anthropic's frontier red team lead said the world must prepare for advanced hacking capabilities to be broadly available within 6, 12 or 24 months; seven months later that transition appears to have arrived on schedule.
insights.speaker: Logan Graham
insights.so_what: A lab's own timeline for capabilities spreading proved accurate, which makes its future proliferation forecasts worth taking seriously.
insights.quote: We need to prepare now for a world where these capabilities are broadly available in 6, 12, 24 months.

insights.claim: Edera's CTO cautions that closed labs have probably trained unreleased models beyond these capabilities, which makes this a cat-and-mouse race to patch vulnerabilities before open models find them.
insights.speaker: Alex Zenla
insights.so_what: Closed labs probably still have an edge at the very top, but it lasts only months.
insights.quote: it is likely that the closed labs have trained additional, unreleased models exceeding these capabilities

insights.claim: Zenla adds that 'abliterated' open models, whose safety training is stripped by modifying weights, make open-weight models capable of advanced attacks today, and warns this may be the start of a dangerous security landscape.
insights.speaker: Alex Zenla
insights.so_what: Safety training on open weights can be removed, so the defense has to come from patching and detection, not from model guardrails.
insights.quote: I do think this may be the beginning of a dangerous security landscape

insights.claim: AI has sped up and scaled vulnerability discovery and network probing for both attackers and defenders this year, but experts still debate whether it is a new kind of threat or an amplifier of existing ones.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: More vulnerabilities found and fixed points to sustained demand for vulnerability-management and patching tools.
insights.locator: Much of the year in cybersecurity

insights.claim: In real-world observation, criminal and state-backed hackers have mostly saved resources by using older, less capable proprietary and open models rather than the frontier.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: The near-term threat comes more from scale than from top-end capability, so frontier parity may change incidents less than the headlines suggest.
insights.quote: attackers are doing what they always do by conserving their resources

insights.claim: Defenders should assume that the best-funded and most motivated attackers have had at least some access to closed models all along, despite strict controls.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: Gated access was never fully secure, so treat sophisticated attackers as already AI-equipped.
